records.notes: Alaska CPAs complete 80 CPE hours per biennial (2-year) licensing period, with at least 20 hours completed in each of the two years, including at least 4 hours of ethics somewhere in the 2-year period (no state-specific ethics course is mandated by regulation -- AICPA Ethics, Circular 230 Ethics, or Behavioral Ethics all qualify). No more than 10 of the 80 hours may come from micro-learning (activities under one hour). Renewal is biennial, due Dec 31 of odd-numbered years. Effective for licensing periods beginning on/after Jan 1, 2026, no more than 12 CPE hours may be earned in a single day. Two independent official sources state the same 80/20/4-hour figures: the Division's own Statutes and Regulations compilation of 12 AAC 04.300, and the Board's own licensee update.

records.citation: 17 CAR § 236-1203 (CPE basic requirements; formerly Board Rule 13.2)
records.notes: Arkansas offers licensees a CHOICE of two equivalent tracks (17 CAR § 236-1203(a), formerly Rule 13.2(a)): 120 hours within the 36 months immediately preceding Jan 1 of the renewal year, OR 40 hours within the 12 months immediately preceding that date. At least 4 hours of CPE in accounting professional conduct/ethics are required every 36 months, and 1 of those 4 hours must specifically be an Arkansas State Board-specific laws-and-rules course (satisfiable via the Board's own free web-based course) -- that 1 hour counts toward, not in addition to, the 4-hour ethics total. New licensees are exempt from the ethics requirement until their first full calendar year of licensure, and CPE hours in the first calendar year of licensure are prorated. Interpretation trap: no more than 80% of total hours may come from self-study/independent-study/authorship combined (17 CAR § 236-1204(f), formerly Board Rule 13.3(f)) -- a detail several vendor summaries omit.

records.notes: Many third-party CPE-vendor sites cite 'Rule 1.9' or '1.10' of 3 CCR 705-1 for Colorado's CPE requirement, but that citation is incorrect -- Rule 1.9 covers professional conduct (independence, conflicts of interest), not CPE hours. The correct rule is 1.6(G)(2): a certificate holder must complete 10 hours of CPE for each full quarter of active licensure during the reporting period (10 x 8 quarters = the 80-hour, 2-year figure the Board's own page states in plain English). Rule 1.6(G)(2)(b) is the ethics sub-clause: 4 of those hours must be in ethics, of which 2 may be in Colorado-rules-and-regulations-specific content (CR&R). No more than 20% of CPE may be in personal development, and no more than 50% in any combination of teaching/publishing. No explicit single-year minimum is stated -- the requirement accrues per-quarter continuously, not as a distinct annual floor like several other states in this cluster.

records.notes: Connecticut's base CPE requirement runs on an ANNUAL cycle rather than the biennial pattern common elsewhere: 40 hours of CPE must be completed each year during the July 1-June 30 period immediately preceding the December 31 reporting/renewal deadline. The ethics requirement, however, does not repeat every year -- 4 hours of ethics (covering the State/National Code of Conduct, Professional Conduct, and licensing regulations) are required only once every 3 consecutive annual CPE cycles, and those hours count toward, not in addition to, that year's 40-hour total. This is an inverted version of the classic 'annual vs. per-cycle' ethics trap (cf. Virginia, where ethics is annual within a multi-year total) -- here the base requirement is annual but ethics is multi-year. CPAs performing attest or compilation services must earn 8 of the annual 40 hours in financial statement preparation/reporting. New licensees are exempt from CPE for their first July-June cycle.

records.citation: 17 D.C.M.R. §§ 2530.1, 2530.8 (D.C. Municipal Regulations, Board of Accountancy)
records.notes: DC CPAs must complete 80 hours of acceptable CPE during the two-year period preceding license renewal (biennial cycle, renewal due Dec 31 of even-numbered years), including no fewer than 4 hours of Professional Ethics instruction (effective since Jan 1, 2005). Both 17 DCMR 2530 and DC's own official CPE Reporting Form (dlcp.dc.gov) state the same 80-hour / 4-hour-ethics requirement; the form cites §§2530.1 and 2530.8 directly. No annual minimum (e.g., 20 hrs/year) is stated in the actual regulation text, despite some CE-vendor sites implying one -- only the 80-hour biennial total and the 4-hour ethics carve-out are codified. Initial renewals of licenses issued for under 2 years are exempt; reinstatement after lapse requires 40 hrs/year of non-renewal up to a 120-hour max (a different, non-recurring figure -- do not confuse with the standard renewal requirement).

records.citation: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 20-11-.02 (Requirements), as amended effective January 1, 2024
records.notes: 80 CPE credits per two-year reporting period, of which at least 50% (40 credits) must be in TECHNICAL fields of study, with a minimum of 20 credits earned each year. 4 ethics credits are required, including 1 credit specific to the laws, rules and policies of the Georgia Board -- that Board-specific hour must come from a Board-approved program; the other 3 may be any behavioral or regulatory ethics. Up to 15 excess NON-technical credits may carry over to the next reporting period, but carryover can never satisfy the technical-fields minimum. Licensees aged 70 or older are exempt. Interpretation trap: a widely-repeated '16 hours in accounting and auditing' figure is the PRE-2024 requirement -- it was replaced on January 1, 2024 by the 50% technical-fields rule, which is more than twice as many credits.

records.data_gap_note: Georgia has two official versions of this rule in circulation and they do not agree. The Secretary of State's rules site (rules.sos.ga.gov/gac/20-11) still serves the PRE-2024 text -- 80 hours with 16 in accounting and auditing, and no ethics requirement at all. The Board's own published Rule 20-11, effective January 1, 2024, is the current one and is what this record follows. If you look the rule up on the Secretary of State's site and see different numbers, that is why; confirm with the Board.

records.citation: Haw. Code R. §§ 16-71-2, 16-71-33 (Hawaii Administrative Rules, Board of Public Accountancy)
records.notes: Hawaii CPAs/permit holders must complete at least 80 hours of CPE within the 24-month period preceding a biennial permit renewal (renewal due Dec 31 of odd-numbered years), with a minimum of 20 hours earned within each calendar year, and at least 4 of the 80 hours must be in ethics or professional conduct (these 4 hours also simultaneously satisfy the separate license-renewal ethics attestation under §16-71-2). These figures are stated in HAR §§16-71-2 and 16-71-33. Maximum carryover of excess hours to the next biennium is 40 hours; new CPAs get 80 hours of automatic CPE credit for passing the AICPA exam (or 40 hours if claimed in year 3).

records.citation: Miss. Admin. Code, Title 30, Pt. 1, Rule 4.1 (Compliance Requirements and Reporting)
records.notes: Mississippi's base CPE requirement is ANNUAL, not triennial: a minimum of 40 CPE credit hours within each one-year (12-month) compliance period ending June 30 (up to 20 excess hours may carry over into the next annual period). Layered WITHIN that annual cycle is a separate TRIENNIAL ethics component: a minimum of 3 hours of Board-approved Ethics and Professional Conduct plus a separate minimum of 1 hour of Mississippi Public Accountancy Law and Regulations, every 3 years (current cycle July 1, 2025-June 30, 2028) -- 4 ethics-related hours total, but on a 3-year cadence inside the annual 40-hour requirement, not 4 hours per year on top of it. Interpretation trap: multiple vendor pages (and even a preliminary MSBPA search snippet) conflate this into a flat '120 hours per rolling 3-year period,' which is mathematically consistent (40 x 3) but obscures that compliance is actually checked and reported annually, not triennially. New licensees are exempt from CPE in their initial (partial) compliance period and from the ethics/law requirement for the rest of that triennial cycle. Both Rule 4.1 and the Mississippi State Board's own CPE page state the same 40-hour annual / 3-plus-1-hour triennial ethics structure.

records.notes: Wyoming certificate holders must complete 120 CPE credits over a rolling 3-year period once fully phased in (0 credits owed at the first renewal, 60 credits over the first 2 years at the second renewal, then 120 over 3 years at every subsequent renewal). At least 66% of required hours (80 of 120) must be in technical subject categories. Separately, all four ethics credits must be completed at least once every 3-year period, all four in the same calendar year, using a Board-approved course that includes a Wyoming statutes-and-rules element. Non-obvious trap: for a brand-new certificate holder, the 4-hour Wyoming ethics course is due within 6 months of the initial permit -- a much faster, separate deadline from the standard 3-year ethics cycle that applies afterward. Confirmed independently by the codified rule text (Chapter 5, §5-3, via Cornell LII) and the Board of CPAs' own CPE page (cpaboard.wyo.gov).
